#3248. Serve Robotics (SERV) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Delivery volume tripled, yet one platform partner's decline is a point management flagged.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Serve Robotics Inc. (SERV +38.79%) reported a 313% increase in third-quarter revenue and raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $12 million. Management attributed the growth to increased delivery volume with partners DoorDash and Grubhub and improvements in fleet margins through cost reduction programs. The company introduced Physical AI services to offer its data and software infrastructure to other robot manufacturers while expanding its geographic footprint into Gold Coast, Australia. Management indicated that the company's $198 million in liquidity supports ongoing research and development in autonomy and the development of the Moxi 2.0 platform for healthcare applications.

Operator: Hello, and thank you for standing by. My name is Temi and I'll be your conference operator today. At this time, I would like to welcome everyone to Serve Robotics, Inc. Third quarter 2026 Financial Results and Conference Call. [Operator Instructions]. I would now like to turn the conference over to Steve Webb, you may begin.

Steve Webb: Thank you, operator. Welcome to Serve Robotics Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Call. With me today are Serve's Co-Founder and CEO, Ali Kashani; and our CFO, Brian Read. During today's call, we may present both GAAP and non-GAAP financial measures. If needed, a reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP measures can be found in our earnings release filed earlier today. Certain statements in this call are forward-looking statements. You should not place undue reliance on forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially from these forward-looking statements and we do not undertake any obligation to update any forward-looking statements we make today, except as required by law.

For more information about factors that may cause actual results to differ materially from forward-looking statements, please refer to the press release we issued today as well as the risks and uncertainties described in our most recent annual report on Form 10-K as supplemented by our most recent quarterly report on Form 10-Q and in other reports and filings made with the SEC. We published our quarterly financial press release and our updated corporate presentation to our Investor Relations website earlier today, and we ask you to review those documents if you haven't already. And with that, let me hand it over to Ali.

Ali Kashani: Thank you, Steve, and good afternoon, everyone. We delivered third quarter revenue of $2.8 million ahead of our expectations and up over 300% year-over-year. We are also raising our full year 2026 revenue guidance to $12 million, which is from the previous guidance of $9 million to $10 million. That is an almost 30% increase. We are really encouraged by how the team is executing. We've been focused on broadening our demand for robots and also improving our economics for the business. And this quarter, the results show that our efforts are paying off.

Our goal is to use Physical AI to make local delivery more affordable for merchants and consumers and we are working towards that by making our network easier to access and also expanding into new markets and geographies while also lowering our cost of operating the robots and generating more revenue from each robot. So let's start with our newer platform partners, where we are seeing a lot of delivery growth from DoorDash and Grubhub. Daily deliveries with them has more than tripled from the end of Q2 to the end of Q3, and the share of all deliveries has more than doubled in the same quarter.

Also, the number of merchants from the new platforms grew over 2.5x over the same period, and it continues to scale. These partnerships give us multiple paths to delivery growth. We're really focused on turning that broader merchant base into more work for our robots. The growth that we are seeing in the delivery side is actually underpinned by the continuous improvements we are making to our technology. Currently, our robots are 13% faster than they were in Q2. That is a 13% speed up in just a few months. The robots now travel 7% more miles per delivery, meaning that they can cover more business to perform a timely dropoff. Our reliability is another key to unlocking this growth.

Our delivery completion rate was 99.9% in Q3 as it was in Q2. That means that of every 1,000 deliveries we pick up, 999 are delivered to the consumer successfully and no tip needed. Advances in our Level 4 autonomy are helping our robots move faster, and they're also reducing their staffing costs needed to support them. So stay tuned because we have some big announcements about our autonomy in the coming weeks. Now alongside these technical advancements, we've also been reducing our day-to-day operating cost for the fleet. We delivered results on a slate of cost reduction programs in the quarter that benefited our cost per delivery. And in aggregate, they saved us about $1 million in the quarter.

Let me give you a couple of examples. First one is the improvements we made to our procurement and maintenance programs to drive significant efficiencies when it comes to robot repairs and replacement parts. The second is how we streamline the way we deploy robots every day, we made them faster and less expensive. And this cuts the external cost of deployment by 75%. Taken together, these efforts improved fleet margin by over 100 percentage points from Q2 to Q3. Now in order to build on our growth momentum, we are making our delivery network easier to access. Our relationship with Wonder and Grubhub has added another channel for demand in markets such as Washington, D.C. metro area.

We are also working directly with merchants through Beacon, which is what we announced last quarter. Beacon allows us to integrate seamlessly with more merchants, and we are seeing great progress with the initiative. We recently launched our first beacon-enabled locations in San Antonio, Texas. The easier we make it for others to use our network, the more potential there is for them to bring their own ideas and their own customers. We know our fleet can support users and use cases beyond what we've developed ourselves. So we'll have more to share as some of these opportunities open up.

Another important foundation for growth is our geographic reach to enable rapid growth, we have to have really robust playbooks for deploying to new markets. We have to have mature AI and autonomy models that can easily adapt to new cities and countries, and we have to have regulatory and policy support to launch new geos. So we have developed these robust playbooks now for expansion and policy and have matured our AI models after scaling to more than 20 cities in the U.S. So we are now taking these learnings into new international markets. and we are able to get operational in new cities with less friction.

Last week, we announced our launch in Gold Coast Australia, a market that we are really excited about. Gold Coast is our first international market expansion and is in an exclusive partnership with DoorDash. In our early deployments using this strategy, we are expecting to launch cities with 1/5 the cost and in a fraction of the time required compared to our legacy deployment formats. We are pretty excited about the results so far and continue to invest heavily into this.

Lower costs are one part of the evolution of our fleet economics. Another way to make local automated logistics more affordable is by increasing robot monetization beyond delivery fees. You've heard me discuss this before, but this actually helps us diversify our revenues. And one really good example for this is branding. Hospitals and sidewalks are very different and unpredictable environment, but both of them forced us to solve these practical problems of robots operating among people in diverse and challenging environments.

Besides our years of work on onboard AI and autonomous fleet software have also generated data and operating experience that other companies are asking us to use inbound inquiries about our foundation model data are increasing, and we are beginning to serve our first customer. Our robust experience real-world edge cases and gather insights every day across a range of environments and scenarios that we believe makes us quite unique in the marketplace.

It's early, but the cities, as a tipping point for building another path for the work our robot already do to generate value which is to help accelerate the Physical AI revolution by teaching foundation models about the real world. This interest we are seeing extends beyond just data. It also extends to our technologies that power are robots. New robot forms are being developed across many industries, and we want to help them come to commercial scale faster. That's why we are not just stopping with 7 Moxy robots. To sum up, we delivered Q3 revenue ahead of expectations.

We are raising our full year outlook from $9 million to $10 million to $12 million and we are advancing our technology, making our robots faster and more reliable than ever. We are reaching more merchants and expanding domestically and internationally while at the same time, also lowering the cost of operating our robots and improving gross margins. Ali Kashani: We've done groceries in the past with -- directly with merchants in Los Angeles, for example. And yes, it's definitely a market we've been paying attention to. And as you know, we have relationship with DoorDash. So I believe this is going to take them about a year or 2 to close, if I recall the process. So it might be a while, but we'll be very excited to speak to them and see if the opportunities there.

Operator: Next question comes from the line of Jeffrey Cohen with Ladenburg.

Jeffrey Cohen: Could you talk a bit about Beacon and some early experience as far as the rollouts there as far as San Antonio? And maybe talk about some of the providers and what you're finding as far as optimization and how we may see that expand?

Ali Kashani: Yes. Yes, happy to take that, Jeff. So we have our first merchants now using Beacon. This is just for folks who may not remember, we talked about it more advance in the last earnings. It's a small tablet that enables merchants to get notifications and a robot is doing their deliveries. It's off the pretty big bottlenecks when we are trying to integrate with more restaurants, especially when you -- when they using POS systems, and we want to try to have a direct relationship with them. So it's still early days for that, but it's pretty important missing piece of the puzzle that we've now brought to the table.

So I expect we would see more adoption over time.

Jeffrey Cohen: Okay. And then secondly, as a follow-up, could you talk about Moxi a little bit and the 2.0 development and maybe it gives us a flavor of commercial and sales channels and existing in new hospitals as far as POs and your sales organization.

Ali Kashani: Yes. So the 2026 was really an investment year for Moxi. So we did the acquisition at the beginning of the year, we invested and help build a new Moxi 2.0 hardware. With that now rolling out, we are hoping to kind of switch into both getting the current fleet upgraded, but also getting them into new hospitals. And there are definitely conversations with partners and distributors about what 2027 and 2028 is going to look like. So I'm hoping to have more to say about that in the coming months.

Operator: Next question comes from the line of Andres Sheppard with Cantor Fitzgerald.

Unknown Analyst: This is Peter on for Andres. Congrats on the quarter. So first, we were hoping you could spend a little bit more on the Uber relationship. Do you think there's maybe an opportunity to resume this partnership in the future?

Ali Kashani: Peter. I don't have much new here. The relationship continues right now. We still are doing our contracts, which goes, I believe, through part of Q1 next year. And I don't have anything that has changed. We'll kind of continue to evaluate that as time goes by. But I guess just worth mentioning where we are seeing a lot of growth and momentum that we Grubhub are daily delivery growth. Something about 60% to 70% just in the last month. And I mentioned DoorDash as well, something like tripled in daily volume.

So it's a really good growth with our newer partners and then we'll see how things go to be, but I think it's been fairly transparent about what you're thinking as of last quarter.

Unknown Analyst: Got it. Very helpful. And then maybe you had -- when we're heading into 2027, can you talk a little bit more about some of the operational goals, whether you be targeting more increased utilization of your existing fleet or looking to scale up the number of your bots deployed?

Ali Kashani: Yes. So I think we are always pushing three things at the same time here. So first one is just improving the technology. So I mentioned that we have increased the speed of robots just since Q2 by something like 13%, which is really phenomenal progress there. Also, there's going to be some big announcement we have coming out about autonomy. So we're going to keep pushing the technology, and that has downstream impacts on the operation as well. On the scale, as we are building demand, especially with new partners, I mentioned how we have more than doubled the number of merchants with Grubhub and merchant in the last quarter.

So we are going to see opportunities perhaps for more robots or new neighborhoods, new cities. And then the third pillar here is always cost down. So just getting better at operation and driving the cost of operations down. And you can see again in this quarter, we made good progress there too.

Tech > Services & Software > Online > Online Services

These free Google alternatives make it easy to break up with the tech giant.

On Tuesday, Nov. 3, Google announced that starting next year AI tools will be turned off by default in software used by K-12 students. Teachers and administrators will have to enable the features for students to use them in Google Search.

“Search and AI are deeply integrated,” Chris Phillips, vice president for education at Google, said, according to the New York Times. He also said if a school bans Google’s AI tools, students “will not have access to Search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.”

If you’re a parent or educator, you should know you don’t have to use Google Search to teach your children. There are plenty of other free search engines you can try now.

It’s also important to note that using these search engines in Google Chrome may prevent you from getting their full benefits. Here are five free alternatives to Google Search.

Brave also offers other features, like a VPN, a crypto wallet and its own AI assistant named Leo. And Brave said your AI usage is private and secure as well. You don’t even need to create or log into an account to use Leo.

This private, Berlin-based search engine is also a green option. Ecosia writes online it has planted over 250 million trees and produces more clean energy than it takes to power all its searches and AI queries. The company also writes online that all its profits go toward climate action.

This French-based search engine writes online it doesn’t retain your search data or sell your personal data, making it a good alternative to Google. In addition to search, Qwant also offers a feature called Qwant Junior, which it writes online is meant to help children between the ages of 6 and 12 years old safely explore the internet.

You should know that Qwant has integrated AI into its engine in what it calls Flash Answers. But you can deactivate it from your Settings menu without jumping through hoops. Historically, Qwant has used Bing’s search API, which lets companies access Bing’s search infrastructure. But according to CNBC, the company partnered with Berlin-based search engine Ecosia in 2024 to build a European search index in order to reduce dependence on US companies.

Startpage is a search engine that’s also a search aggregator. That means it partners with other companies like Google and Microsoft Bing to bring you search results.

For more on other search engines, here’s what to know about DuckDuckGo and Brave Search.

#3246. Want an AI job? Deployment engineers are earning executive-level pay – up to $1.45M a year

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

AI has ushered in new jobs, and some of them are paying handsomely, according to a new study.

AI engineers are making well over six figures in salary — and plenty more in bonuses and equity, according to data from a new report by executive search firm Christian & Timbers.

Enterprises now pay “elite” AI deployment engineers between $586,000 and $1.45 million annually in total compensation, with senior leaders in the field earning up to $2.25 million, according to the report. This figure approaches the median compensation of executive officers of public companies, the authors note.

Also: ‘So perfect, they are literally identical’ – Your AI-polished resumes are recruiters’ new top stressor

Christian & Timbers is an AI executive search and leadership advisory firm, recruiting CEOs, board members, technology executives, and AI engineers for enterprises. The new report draws on more than 550 interviews with engineers, deployment leaders, and executives conducted from January through June 2026, along with closed and current open offers. The compensation bands are Christian & Timbers’ estimates and represent ranges rather than statistical averages.

“Enterprise CEOs are under pressure to deliver returns for their AI investments. The most important decision is how to build the team that delivers on that goal,” said Jeff Christian, founder and CEO of Christian & Timbers, in a press release.

Also: What workers are really using AI for in 2026 – and what they aren’t

The report noted that the staggering salary range includes base salary, bonus, and annualized equity. Christian & Timbers said it defines an “elite” forward deployment engineer (FDE) as “a senior AI-native deployment builder, typically with 7 to 15 years of experience, including at least two years building and deploying agentic automated workflows that deliver measurable ROI with a documented enterprise impact of $10M or more,” who has also led a team of other forward deployment engineers.

Also: 50% of companies generate value from AI now – here’s how

The large salary ranges reflect increasing enterprise investments in AI talent and employee development. Microsoft, AWS, and OpenAI have announced more than $7.5 billion in corporate and partner investment in AI deployment over the past six months, Christian & Timbers noted in the release.

Also: Nearly 70% of workers use AI regularly now – but many get no time to upskill

There’s an increasing need to fill roles such as Senior Principal AI Engineer, AI Solutions Engineer, and Head of Deployment — but there is a limited pool of qualified candidates. The firm estimates that only 2,000 of the most senior deployment leaders exist in the US market, according to a previous Christian & Timbers study, which does not meet demand — so companies are competing for the same small group of professionals, hence the increasing salaries.

While the report underscores lucrative yields for certain engineering roles, the firm said that public job titles make comparisons more challenging.

“Christian & Timbers’ elite category spans several titles, while advertised FDE roles cover a broader range of experience and responsibilities. Experienced deployment engineers may be recruited directly or promoted into the work under titles such as staff software engineer or principal AI engineer,” the study said.

Plus, equity and bonus make up 52% to 66% of senior engineer pay, and most job postings don’t include that value in the salary, the report noted.

#3244. If the White House Network Can Be Hijacked by Proxies, Your Smart Home Is Already at Risk

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Tech > Services & Software > Cybersecurity

A new report finds residential proxies exiting the White House network 236 times in the past month.

As if the Trump administration needed any more bad news this week, cybersecurity researchers discovered several residential proxy services originating from the White House network, exposing a potential security flaw that could allow cybercriminals to route traffic through official government IP addresses.

The security firm Layer3 Intel detected residential proxy activity on AS2650, a network registered to the Executive Office of the President. Another security firm identified software from the proxy server Infatica, a company owned by a Russian entrepreneur who ran a server-rental company used by hackers in attacks on election systems in Arizona and Illinois in 2016.

While there’s no evidence that proxy access was used to carry out attacks on the White House, experts say it could open the door for hackers to exploit vulnerabilities or grant outsiders an unmonitored back door into high-security systems.

“It basically gives them a foothold on a network where previously nobody was getting into the White House network,” Layer3 founder Sergiy Usatyuk told CNET. “From a security policy perspective, it gives you all types of potential pathways to exploit.” (Usatyuk pleaded guilty to federal charges in 2019 for his role in operating websites that launched denial-of-service, or DDoS, attacks.)

Residential proxy services route internet traffic through consumer devices (such as smartphones, laptops or home routers) to make it appear that the activity is being performed by a real person. While proxies can be used for relatively benign purposes — web scraping is by far the most common use case — they’re also popular for activities like malware attacks, identity theft and creating fake social media accounts.

For example, earlier this year, Synthient, another company that tracks proxies and VPNs, documented how one botnet infected more than 2 million devices using a residential proxy server. If a similar vulnerability existed in the White House proxy, hackers could probe the infected device’s internal systems and install malicious payloads.

In its report, Layer3 found traffic from six distinct IP addresses exiting the White House network from at least 28 known residential proxy services between Oct. 5 and Nov. 3, with most activity occurring in the evenings between 5 p.m. and midnight EST. This suggests the culprit may be an employee who connected a personal device to a Wi-Fi network with a compromised app or a proxy SDK (software development kit) running in the background. Third-party SDKs can convert a device into a “proxy node.”

Commercial proxy networks sell access to these nodes, so anyone with a few dollars could rent a trusted IP address — in this case, making it appear as though traffic originates from the Executive Office of the President.

Researchers at Synthient provided more details about the case, posting on X that several White House staffers are running “a Windows 11 machine with InfaticaSDK installed.” They pointed directly to Rave, a popular app that lets users watch streaming services with friends, as the likely delivery mechanism for the residential proxy traffic detected on the White House network.

Riley Kilmer, co-founder of the cybersecurity firm Spur Intelligence, wrote in a LinkedIn post that different types of proxy companies had been discovered in the White House, including one called 9Proxy, which is often used by criminals for banking fraud.

The White House didn’t respond to CNET’s request for comment.

Because smart TVs, connected appliances and home routers usually have minimal user oversight, a single unvetted app or out-of-date firmware update can turn a household of IoT devices into an exit node for commercial proxy networks.

Proxies can generally “glom” onto consumer devices by embedding networking code directly into software, either consensually (users willingly install it) or nonconsensually (by exploiting unsecured device access points).

It starts when app developers look for revenue by integrating those proxy SDKs into their free apps. Then, when you install the app, the fine print of the terms and conditions of service often includes a clause that allows the app to add your IP address to a third-party proxy pool.

A June report from Spur Intelligence found that roughly one in three apps available on Samsung and LG smart TVs were selling users’ IP addresses. To avoid ads, users often accept the terms when downloading the app — a type of unnoticed consent. Once installed, the SDK runs continuously in the background, registering the device’s IP with the proxy provider’s gateway, unless you delete the app or opt out. (The report notes that Amazon and Roku have explicitly banned this practice.)

Using a free VPN could expose you to the same risk, allowing your IP address to be used by someone else for nefarious activities. The FBI’s guidance on protecting yourself against proxies specifically calls out free VPNs as one of the primary ways bad actors gain access to an IP address.

In some cases, you don’t need to download anything to get your IP thrown into a shady proxy pool — you just have to buy the wrong device. A recent investigation by Synthient discovered that more than 1.3 million streaming devices from the China-based device manufacturer MECOOL were infected with proxy SDKs. A proxy service called SocksEscort was charged by the Justice Department in March with compromising thousands of routers to submit fraudulent unemployment insurance claims.

Checking whether your IP address is being used by a proxy service without your knowledge is relatively simple. Layer3 provides a free proxy-checking tool that searches its database of over 70 million proxies to find if yours is listed. GreyNoise, another cybersecurity company, also offers a free IP-checking service.

These tools can tell you if proxy traffic is passing through your network, but they can’t identify which specific device has the SDK running. You’ll have to do some additional detective work to figure out the culprit. Some common sources include free VPNs, gaming apps, “one price, no subscriptions” streaming boxes and smart TVs.

Cybersecurity experts also recommend keeping the firmware on all your internet-connected devices up to date and downloading only from trusted app stores.

#3243. Researchers asked people to use AI chatbots for election info – results were mixed

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Chatbots can skew election-related information and act as an intervening layer in a voter's search.

Most search tools now put a layer of AI between you and the information you’re looking for, especially Google.

Also: Tired of AI Overviews? I found 9 Google Search alternatives

In a new study, Yale researchers found that a third of users asked a chatbot to help them pick a candidate. Grok often recommended candidates on its own without any information from users, while ChatGPT recommended candidates most often overall, and twice as much as Claude.

The researchers asked nearly 2,500 people in 35 states with Senate races to query ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, or Gemini about the election. Participants in the study, which ran for a few weeks in October leading up to the Nov. 3 midterm elections, were adults who already use chatbots weekly.

Most users asked chatbots for basic facts about the election, including who was on the ballot. But 36% asked a chatbot to help them pick a candidate to vote for, often by describing their priorities and asking the chatbot to assess which candidates aligned with them.

The former query has slightly less room for error, because the internet has a ton of data on the basic facts of an election, such as who is running where. Chatbots interpreting candidate positions, on the other hand, is a bit more dicey, and relies significantly on the sources a chatbot uses (a statement from a candidate’s own website, for example, is more reliable than a social media clip of an opponent characterizing them in a certain way).

Also: How to keep your chatbot conversations as private as possible

In one example, a user asked ChatGPT to give them the “pros and cons” of each candidate in Virginia, an inherently subjective question.

When it came to recommending candidates, chatbots varied widely.

“When users asked who to vote for but had not yet said anything about themselves, only Grok regularly recommended a candidate, in 14% of chats,” the researchers wrote. “Once users shared their views, ChatGPT recommended a candidate in 79% of chats and Claude in 40%, with Grok and Gemini in between.”

Pew Research found that 42% of US adults surveyed use chatbots to search for information. That’s a broad umbrella that can include election information — but Pew also found that only 8% of US adults reported using chatbots to find election-related information in this year’s election.

What those users are looking for matters, though. Pew found that of that group, 76% were inquiring about where candidates stand on certain issues, and 71% were fact-checking information they’d heard about candidates or issues.

Also: OpenAI will merge ChatGPT’s chat and work tabs

Given that chatbots are still not reliable summarizers, the nature of these questions poses a misinformation risk if users don’t also check a chatbot’s linked sources. An overwhelming majority of users don’t, at least when it comes to Google’s AI Overviews. At least one study found AI platforms gave users “outdated or inaccurate” information that could mislead voters in some cases by missing a deadline or failing to mention a step about voting logistics.

This election cycle was particularly plagued by AI-generated deepfakes and misinformation as tools have become much more sophisticated since the 2024 election. OpenAI and Anthropic reportedly set up election “war rooms” to monitor misuse and information accuracy, according to exclusive reporting by Politico and Semafor.

While an August study from the Brennan Center for Justice found that chatbots did push back surprisingly well against certain falsehoods related to election disinformation campaigns, it also found that AI models easily generated “misleading election-related images and video” when asked.

“Many of their safeguards for preventing this were ineffective, inconsistently applied, or functionally absent,” noted the study, which tested ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok, Meta AI, Runway, and Flux.2.

Also: 50 AI agents tried to build a thriving Minecraft civilization – it didn’t end well

Apart from these factors, however, there is a broader theme in AI use that is equally consequential for civic engagement: cognitive offloading. The political media landscape can already be dense and hard to parse for a voter trying to stay informed. Layering a chatbot — which has opaque training data sets, filters, and other settings determined at the discretion of AI labs — on top of that information search process can further muddy the waters while appearing like a convenient and neutral summarizing tool.

While some studies test how AI chatbots respond to election questions by using standardized questions, this approach let users themselves engage with chatbots as they normally would. While the Yale researchers’ queries and standardized study queries show a lot of similarities, the distinction is valuable for evaluations.

“This is a small step toward evaluations that measure AI’s political influence on the questions users actually ask,” the researchers noted.

Outside of users self-reporting what they asked a chatbot, only AI labs have records of what users are really asking about elections. In October, Anthropic analyzed 250,000 conversations with Claude and determined people “rarely ask Claude whom or what to vote for,” finding that “0.51% of all conversations are specifically about elections or voting,” though it expected election-related queries to increase closer to Nov. 3.

Also: 6 AI agent workflows I use to hand off everyday tasks

“More often, we observed people asking Claude questions that could help them reach their own conclusions, like where candidates stand on a particular issue. Requests that violated our election integrity policies were even less common, appearing in about 0.002% of conversations,” Anthropic’s report said.

The Yale researchers said the next step for a study like theirs is determining how accurate and unbiased models are in their responses, as well as what models learn about users, and whether their recommendations actually match users’ needs.

“In multi-turn chats, users often answered the chatbot’s questions, and those answers led to its recommendations. The questions a model asks shape what users tell it and what it recommends,” the researchers explained.

#3241. Is Chrome’s settings menu getting a search bar? What we know

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Chrome might receive a much-needed addition.

I’m a longtime Chrome user, but I’ve never been a fan of the browser’s user settings menu, which has grown into a dense collection of nesting submenus that can be difficult to navigate. That may be changing soon.

Also: How Chrome warns you about suspicious websites now

X (formerly Twitter) user, Leopeva64, posted a short video and several still images showcasing a potential new feature in Chrome Canary, which Google uses to test new Chrome web tools and features. The posts show the search bar pinned to the top of the settings menu for instant access. By entering the name of the submenu or feature you want to access, the new search bar could save a lot of time normally spent clicking around, trying to remember exactly where it’s located.

In Chrome Canary, Google is testing removing the scroll arrows that let you automatically scroll to reveal hidden items when you hover over them in the 3-dot menu. They also added a scrollbar, and the search box at the top and the footer are now pinned so they are always visible: https://t.co/Plx6BgKfJN pic.twitter.com/D7TxDkCtmP

According to Leopeva64, other possible new features include a visual update that groups similar menu options into tiles for faster navigation of your most-accessed settings, as well as pinning the menu footer to keep it visible as you click through.

Chrome Extensions is also up for a possible refresh with a move to a dedicated submenu called Manage Skills to help keep all of your installed extensions organized and make it easier to remove ones that are no longer needed.

Also: How to take full-page screenshots in Chrome on any device – it’s easy and free

Google Lens may get a new submenu, called “Ask Google about this page,” for searching for items you see across an entire page, not just in a single image.

There’s no official word yet on when these features will leave Canary’s testing environment and become available in the regular Chrome menu. I’ve reached out to Google for a comment, but at the time of writing, I have not received a response.

With October in the can, we can finally say goodbye to the Sunday scaries. Hoorah! Now that Netflix’s November 2026 schedule is set, we’ve got plenty of great new content to get stuck into. This week, I’ve gone for a trio of shows that contain mercifully few frights.

First up is the highly-anticipated second season of “Black Doves”, where Keira Knightley continues to shine as the wife of the British Prime Minister… oh, and she’s also a covert spy. Next is the debut of “Will Trent” on Netflix. If you’ve slept on this charming detective drama, you’ve got a whole lot of binge-watching ahead of you this weekend with all four seasons now available. Lastly, season two of “North of North” is streaming, and Siaja’s chilly Canadian misadventures continue to delight.

Whether you're pining for spy thrills or gentle laughs with a detective and his tiny pooch, here are three fresh Netflix releases you should definitely add to your weekend watchlist.

Talk about the best of British. “Black Doves” season 2 rocks an absolutely stellar cast of Blighty greats. Keira Knightley continues to impress as a covert agent who keeps leaking national secrets for the titular spy agency. Naughty Keira! She’s reunited with her handler Mrs. Reed (a typically charismatic Sarah Lancashire), who promptly goes missing, driving much of this season’s plot.

Our secrets-sharing protagonist also gets reacquainted with her best pal Sam (Ben Whishaw), who just so happens to be a professional assassin… and a bit of a drunk. This high-tension drama also benefits from the arrival of “Scream” legend Neve Campbell. Well plotted and stylishly shot, you can tell the Big N has chucked a huge amount at this thriller.

Watch "Black Doves" season 2 on Netflix now

The first four seasons of this detective drama are now available to stream on Netflix, and "Will Trent" really does feel like a love letter to “Monk”. Tipping its hat to Tony Shalhoub’s awkward but brilliant homicide cop, the titular star of this show (played by Ramón Rodríguez) also struggles in social situations due to his dyslexia. Yet there’s no other agent you’d want on your case if you suddenly found your corpse ditched down a drainpipe.

Sign up to the weekly Tom's Streaming Guide to stay in the loop with the latest releases and top recommendations across your favorite streaming services. We’ve got you covered with a complete guide on what’s worth watching.

Much of the action of “Will Trent” focuses on whether our hero can Sherlock his way through various Atlanta-based crimes. But the real hook beyond your standard police procedural tropes? That would be Will’s relationship with a newly adopted chihuahua called Bluebell. This easy going show has serious “Turner & Hooch” vibes. I’m all in.

Watch "Will Trent" seasons 1-4 on Netflix now

Talk about a perfect show for these dark winter months. Focused on Ice Cove, Nunavut, this breezy comedy is set in Canada’s northernmost territory, meaning there’s a whole lot of daylight action. We’re once again back with Siaja (Anna Lambe), a young mother who’s still trying to figure out life post-divorce. In this second season, romance is back on the table, as our Inuk heroine enters the icy pools of the speed dating scene.

A big part of the show focuses on community, and Siaja now has to deal with new job demands under her boss Helen (Mary Lynn Rajskub, who you might remember as the irrepressible Chloe from “24”). “North of North” doesn’t trade in Jack Bauer breakneck action, but the show’s gentle laughs are occasionally punctuated with low-stakes drama, like a mini water crisis. Easy giggles and gorgeous scenery. What’s not to like?

Ameren Corporation (AEE +0.04%) management reported an updated long-term growth outlook and an expanded capital investment plan driven by regional economic development and grid modernization requirements. The company stated that increasing energy needs from large load customers, particularly data centers in Missouri, necessitate significant additions to generation and transmission infrastructure. Management indicated that its strategic focus remains on maintaining customer affordability through operational process enhancements and cost-allocation mechanisms mandated by state legislation. The company stated it is executing a balanced financing strategy to support its multiyear capital objectives while maintaining its investment-grade credit ratings.

Operator: Good day, everyone. My name is Ryan, and I will be your conference operator today. At this time, I'd like to welcome you all to the Ameren Corporation Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Call. Andrew Kirk: Thank you, and good morning. On the call with me today are Marty Lyons, Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer; Michael Moehn, Group President of our Ameren Utilities; and Lenny Singh, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer; as well as other members of the Ameren management team. We have posted a presentation on the amereninvestors.com homepage that will be referenced by our speakers.

Please refer to the forward-looking statements section in the news release we issued yesterday as well as our SEC filings for more information about the various factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from those anticipated. Lastly, all per share earnings amounts discussed during today's presentation, including earnings guidance, are presented on a diluted basis, unless otherwise noted. Now here's Marty, who will start on Page 4.

Martin Lyons: Thanks, Andrew. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Starting on Page 4 with key highlights. We are well positioned to meet these needs, support expansion and deliver durable value to our customers, communities and shareholders. First, reflecting our strong year-to-date performance and outlook, we have raised our 2026 earnings per share guidance range and issued 2027 earnings per share guidance that represents solid year-over-year growth.

Looking further ahead, we have also raised our long-term growth outlook with expected compound annual earnings per share growth of 8% to 10% from 2027 through 2031. This outlook reflects strong economic development across our service territory, particularly in Missouri, where 2.8 gigawatts of signed electric service agreements underpin our higher sales forecast and increased generation investment plan with additional opportunities in the pipeline. Regional economic growth is also driving incremental investment opportunities in our Transmission segment to connect new generation resources and serve new large load customers.

To meet this increasing energy need, we plan to strategically invest $38.1 billion in energy infrastructure over the next 5 years, which is expected to drive 13.3% compound annual rate base growth from 2026 through 2031. What excites me most about this plan is the opportunity to create lasting value for our customers and communities through a safer, more reliable and more resilient grid while directly supporting a growing economy with more and better jobs. Indeed, our strategy, outlined on Page 5, is centered on delivering value to the customers and communities we serve, including 2.5 million electric and 900,000 natural gas customers across Missouri and Illinois.

By investing in and strengthening our energy infrastructure, advocating for constructive energy policies and continuously optimizing performance to improve service quality, we are delivering on what matters most to our customers, safe, reliable energy at the lowest cost possible. Turning to Page 6. Execution of our strategy is delivering tangible customer benefits. Over time, we have achieved top quartile reliability performance and strong customer service satisfaction. We have also supported tens of billions of dollars in annual economic impact and in 2025 alone, an estimated 63,000 jobs while keeping average residential rates below national and Midwest averages.

And that's before factoring in the significant additional economic impact from the large load and other customer growth our investments facilitate, including significant incremental tax revenue for our communities. Highlighted on Page 7, execution of our strategy has also delivered strong, consistent shareholder results. Since divesting our merchant business in 2013, weather-normalized adjusted earnings per share have grown at a compound annual rate of approximately 7.4%, annual dividends per share have increased 78% and total shareholder return has exceeded 300%, significantly outperforming utility index averages. Looking ahead, we believe continued execution of this strategy, centered on delivering value for customers and communities will continue to drive superior long-term returns for our shareholders. Turning now to Page 8.

Here, we reiterate our strategic priorities for 2026. Targeted, timely infrastructure investments are key to delivering reliable service. As shown on the right, we invested more than $4 billion in energy infrastructure through September to strengthen reliability and resiliency and improve service. The value of continued investment was evident during the third quarter's extreme heat when our infrastructure performed well and our team successfully managed the system through periods of exceptionally high demand, keeping our coworkers safe, homes cool and businesses running. This year's severe weather, with Illinois leading the nation in tornado activity, further underscores the importance of building a stronger, more resilient energy system and having skilled teams in place to operate it safely and reliably.

In 2026 through September, investments in grid automation helped avoid more than 63 million customer outage minutes across both Missouri and Illinois, a tangible example of how infrastructure investment translates into better service. We also made strong progress on many other objectives, which I'll discuss in a moment. Moving to Page 9. Yesterday, we reported third quarter 2026 earnings of $2.42 per share compared to adjusted earnings of $2.17 per share in the third quarter of 2025. The key drivers of our strong third quarter results are outlined on this page. In light of a strong year-to-date performance, we raised our 2026 earnings per share guidance range to $5.35 to $5.55 from our original range of $5.25 to $5.45.

Turning to Page 10 for our 2027 guidance outlook. We have a long track record of strong and consistent earnings per share growth. As we look ahead, we expect this to continue. We expect 2027 earnings to be in the range of $5.70 to $5.90 per share. The midpoint of this range represents 8.4% earnings per share growth compared to our original 2026 earnings guidance midpoint. At Ameren, we are proud to provide the quality of service that is necessary to attract investment and economic growth to our region.

The pipeline of economic development interest within our service territory remains robust across Missouri and Illinois. Our 5-year financial plan laid out today assumes 12.9% compound annual sales growth in Missouri from 2027 through 2031 based on an assumption of 2.9 gigawatts of new load by 2031. This growth assumption, as depicted by the dashed green line on the chart on the right-hand side of this page, is consistent with our preferred resource plan through 2030, which projects a 60% increase in Missouri sales by 2030 from 2027 levels. This growth is supported by the existing 2.8 gigawatts of electric service agreements with sales from those agreements expected to reach full capacity in 2030.

Beyond these signed agreements, our pipeline includes 1.2 gigawatts of projects with construction agreements and an additional 4.4 gigawatts of projects with completed interconnection studies. We were pleased to see one of the projects with a completed interconnection study advance to a construction agreement since our second quarter update. Consistent with the requirements of Missouri Senate Bill 4, large load customers will pay for the power and infrastructure costs driven by their operations. And once their sites are operational, large load customers will contribute to paying fixed costs of the energy grid, providing long-term cost benefits for other customers. Moving then to Page 12 for an update on Missouri's generation plan.

In September, Ameren Missouri filed its 2026 Integrated Resource Plan, updating its 20-year road map to reliably and cost effectively meet customers' energy needs under a range of future conditions. Using an optimal mix of natural gas, solar, energy storage, wind, nuclear and other technologies, our preferred resource plan is designed to serve 3.4 gigawatts of additional demand by 2031 and 5 gigawatts by 2036. To support this growth, the plan calls for accelerating and expanding natural gas generation and battery storage, expanding solar generation and adding fuel cell generation, extending the retirement date of 2 Labadie Energy Center units from 2036 to 2042 and adding new nuclear generation by 2040.

Importantly, the table on this page identifies the preferred resource plan additions included in our 2027 through 2031 capital plan. The 5-year capital plan supports 2.9 gigawatts of incremental load growth by 2031. Preferred plan resources identified as not included in our 5-year capital and rate base growth plans represent potential upside to our outlook as we execute additional electric service agreements. On Page 13, we outline how continued execution of our strategy is expected to drive strong growth over the next 5 years.

Today, we're rolling forward our 5-year capital plan, which now totals $38.1 billion, reflecting significant investment to serve the anticipated load growth I just discussed while strengthening system reliability. We expect these investments to drive 13.3% compound annual rate base growth from 2026 through 2031. Leveraging our proven strategy and building upon our track record of strong earnings growth, we expect to deliver 8% to 10% compound annual earnings per share growth from 2027 through 2031, using our 2027 guidance midpoint of $5.80 per share as the base. As large load sales ramp in 2028 and 2029, we expect annual earnings per share growth near the upper end of that range in those years.

We also expect to deliver strong, sustainable annual dividend growth as our earnings grow with a payout ratio ranging between 45% to 55%. As we invest to support meaningful economic growth in our communities, our focus remains on delivering reliable, affordable service for all customers with large load customers paying the cost required to serve their operations. I'm truly excited about the opportunity to support this significant growth and the lasting benefits it can bring to local communities and across our region. Michael Moehn: Thanks, Marty, and good morning, everyone. I'll begin on Page 15. As Marty outlined, significant economic development is driving growing energy needs across our region. Our economic development teams remain focused on supporting long-term business investment and job growth. That work is translating into tangible results for our communities. During the second quarter, Google and Amazon announced projects in our Missouri service territory, representing a combined planned investment of $25 billion. These projects are part of the 2.8 gigawatts of ESAs we signed earlier this year. As you can see from the photos on this page, the projects are well underway.

We will continue to work closely with businesses interested in locating operations in our service territory to find the right solutions to meet their energy needs and ultimately support economic development in the region. As our generation investment grows, we are applying lessons learned across projects through a disciplined portfolio-based execution model. This includes standardizing designs and equipment as appropriate, securing long lead components early, leveraging experienced engineering and construction partners across multiple projects and strengthening our internal team to provide consistent oversight.

Work underway at the Castle Bluff and Big Hollow Energy Centers is helping establish a repeatable execution model for other projects, including the 2.1 gigawatt West Alton Energy Center. This approach is designed to improve productivity, better coordinate resources across projects and increase schedule and cost predictability. We believe this approach positions us well to effectively execute future generation projects and meet increasing customer demand. Turning to Page 17. The execution focus we just discussed is critical as we advance Ameren Missouri's broader generation plan.

Consistent with our 2026 preferred resource plan, we are developing a balanced and diverse portfolio that includes adding approximately 7.7 gigawatts of new generation capacity from 2027 through 2031, which would increase Ameren Missouri's installed capacity by approximately 80%. With 5.3 gigawatts of announced projects, we are making tangible progress towards that target. Approximately 2.3 gigawatts of simple cycle gas, solar and battery storage resources have received regulatory approval, are under construction and are expected to begin serving customers in 2027 and 2028. In July, we filed a CCN request for the 2.1 gigawatt West Alton facility, which is expected to be in service in 2031.

In October, the Missouri PSC approved CCN request for nearly 1 gigawatt of solar and storage resources following a 5-month review. These projects are expected to begin serving customers in 2028 and 2029. With more than 5 gigawatts of new generation resources in progress and more in the pipeline, I'm pleased to say that our teams are well positioned to deliver these projects on schedule for our customers. Planned generation additions are expected to generate approximately $2.75 billion of tax credits from 2027 through 2031, providing significant savings for our customers.

As new large load electric demand evolves, our focus remains on serving all our customers reliably and affordably by carefully planning and executing grid upgrades, maintaining a balanced generation portfolio and ensuring costs to serve new large load customers are appropriately allocated to such customers in accordance with Senate Bill 4. Moving to Page 18 for a transmission update. We continue making robust investment in our region's transmission infrastructure to ensure ongoing reliability and efficiency. We expect our transmission investment levels to remain strong over time to support new large load customers and to connect the generation resources required to serve our territory reliably as regional demand grows.

At the same time, we remain focused on executing our assigned and awarded long-range transmission projects for the first 2 MISO LRTP tranches. Notably, we have won the opportunity to develop all 5 competitive long-range transmission projects in our service territory within both the Tranche 1 and Tranche 2 portfolios, reflecting our strong record of delivering high-quality transmission infrastructure at a competitive cost. Over half of the approximate $500 million investment opportunity is included in the capital plan issued today. We recognize that our critical infrastructure projects represent significant investments, which is why we prioritize the projects that are most beneficial for customers and maintain a sharp focus on keeping rates as low as possible. In addition, Ameren invests hundreds of millions of dollars each year to support our customers and communities through energy efficiency programs and demand response initiatives. We've also implemented initiatives designed to strengthen the efficiency of our third-party spend. And also underway, we're working to improve the productivity of our gas operations through standardized operating practices and optimize crew deployment, streamlining operating costs while maintaining strong safety, service and emergency response performance.

We're also advancing a multiyear digital road map to optimize operating costs, simplify the technology landscape and position the company to leverage automation and AI capabilities more effectively. I'm excited by the operational milestones achieved to date, and I'm confident in our team's ability to effectively execute our investment plans in a way that benefits our customers and communities. Leonard Singh: Thanks, Michael. I'll begin on Page 22 of our presentation. These positive factors were partially offset by higher operations and maintenance expenses at Ameren Missouri, primarily driven by increased reliability focused efforts. Moving to Page 26 for an update on Ameren Illinois regulatory matters. 2025 annual reconciliation proceeding under the electric multiyear rate plan continues to progress.

The $28 million adjustment we are requesting reflects 2025 actual cost, actual year-end rate base and the allowed return on equity and common equity ratio established in the multiyear rate plan. Notably, our requested adjustment is aligned with the ICC staff and administrative law judge's recommendations. An ICC decision is expected in December with the approved reconciliation adjustment reflected in rates in 2027. Moving to the Ameren Illinois multiyear grid plan proceeding. We proposed a $2.7 billion electric distribution investment plan for 2028 through 2031. The plan is designed to strengthen grid safety, reliability and resiliency while preparing the system to support evolving customer needs and Illinois' clean energy objectives.

Turning to Page 27. We look at our company-wide capital plan for the next 5 years. As Marty highlighted, we see robust investment opportunities ahead. The plan we are releasing today calls for $38.1 billion in capital expenditures from 2027 through 2031, an increase of more than 20% compared to our capital plan issued last year.

We expect this investment to drive 13.3% compound annual rate base growth from 2026 to 2031, which is outlined by business segment on this page. Turning to Pages 28 and 29, where we provide a financing update.

We continue to feel good about our financial position. As we fund our robust infrastructure plan, we remain focused on maintaining a strong balance sheet and strong credit metrics. Our primary source of funding will continue to be cash from operations, which we expect to increase as sales grow and rates are updated to reflect our investment in energy infrastructure. Additional funding needs will be financed in a balanced manner, consistent with our past practices. We fulfilled our 2026 equity needs in 2025, primarily through $600 million of forward sales agreements that we expect to settle near the end of the year.

We expect to issue approximately $5 billion of equity from 2027 through 2031 and have sold forward in 2026, approximately $1.7 billion of common stock under our at-the-market program to address a portion of those needs. We've had success utilizing our ATM program and expect to continue to leverage the program going forward. We appreciate the flexibility our ATM provides, including the ability to effectively dollar cost average our issuances over time. Based on our anticipated investment and other funding needs, we expect equity issuances for 2027 through 2031 to be concentrated primarily near year-end 2027 and year-end 2028. Long-term debt will fund remaining cash requirements.

In 2027, we expect approximately $5.2 billion of new long-term issuance to refinance maturing obligations and fund a portion of our $8.8 billion of planned investments. A portion of such issuances could include parent company hybrid debt securities, which receive 50% equity credit from Moody's and S&P. Expected timing for 2027 debt issuances is shown on Page 29. We will continue to proactively manage interest rate risk associated with planned parent company new issuances through systematic execution of our rate hedging program. As a reminder, this past spring, S&P and Moody's reaffirmed our stable outlook and BBB+ and Baa1 credit ratings, respectively.

As we've said before, we value our current ratings and remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and strong credit metrics as we execute our growth plan. Moving to Page 30 of our presentation. Marty outlined our 2027 earnings per share guidance range earlier. Expected 2027 earnings detailed by segment compared to our 2026 expectations are highlighted on this page. Robust planned infrastructure investments, strong expected sales and economic growth and strategic business process optimization opportunities give us confidence in our ability to deliver strong earnings growth in 2027 and the years ahead. In summary, turning to Page 31.

We're excited about the opportunities ahead and confident in our ability to execute our strategic plan and deliver strong, sustainable value to customers, communities and shareholders. As Marty noted earlier, our outlook includes 8% to 10% compound annual EPS growth from 2027 through 2031, and we expect EPS growth near the upper end of that range in 2028 and 2029. This anticipated growth reflects strong economic development with expected 12.9% compound annual sales growth in Missouri from 2027 through 2031 as well as our $38.1 billion 5-year capital plan that is expected to drive 13.3% compound annual rate base growth. Additional electric service agreements and the infrastructure investments needed to serve that demand represent potential upside to these growth expectations.

Over the next decade, we have identified an investment pipeline greater than $90 billion needed to support reliability and anticipated economic growth while delivering meaningful benefits to our customers. We also expect to deliver strong sustainable annual dividend growth as our earnings grow with a payout ratio ranging between 45% to 55%. As we execute our robust growth plan, we remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and strong investment-grade credit ratings. Taken together, we believe our strong growth outlook, disciplined financing plan, and focus on operational excellence and execution position us well to deliver long-term value for our customers and competitive total returns for shareholders. With that, we'll now open the call for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question will come from Shar Pourreza with Wells Fargo.

Andrew Kadavy: Actually, it's Andrew Kadavy on for Shar. So looking at the EPS rate CAGR and then also the rate base CAGR, we've seen a big delta there. It's -- the delta has gone up since your last update. Can you talk about what's driving that? Is it structural? Or is this something that could be narrowed through time?

Martin Lyons: Yes. Look, similar to the past, the big delta between the rate base growth and the earnings per share growth rate that we expect has to do with our financing activities. And as you know, we're going to finance the capital expenditure plan that we have, the $38.1 billion capital plan in a very balanced way, consistent with the way we've historically financed our operations, which means we will be issuing some equity over time to help with the financing of that. Today, we talked about the fact that we expect about $5 billion of equity issuances over the next 5 years. We've already got $1.7 billion of that priced through some of the forward hedging that we've done.

But that equity dilution is the primary driver of the difference between the rate base growth plans that we have and the EPS growth that we expect to be able to deliver over the next 5 years.

Andrew Kadavy: And then moving on to the rate case in Missouri. Are you thinking that you'll be able to settle that case? Or since it's, kind of, the first one with a large load tariff involved, maybe you want to fully litigate it? And then on top of that, what kind of outcome are you embedding in your plans for that rate case?

Martin Lyons: Yes, I'll start. This is Marty again and see if anybody else wants to chime in. But we're really still in the very early stages with respect to that rate review. As we indicated in our prepared remarks, this case is really about infrastructure investments that have been made to serve all of our existing customers. Today, we really aren't serving any large loads. We expect those sales to begin ramping up in late 2027, and only modestly in late 2027 and really not ramp up until '28 or '29. So really, this case is really all about infrastructure investments we've made for our traditional customer base.

We expect, as we mentioned, to see direct testimony from parties in early December. So we haven't seen any of that yet. However, we do always try to work with the parties in these cases to resolve issues, and we have a good track record of being able to settle these rate reviews in the past, and that would be our ambition again as we go into this rate review. So typically, those settlements have occurred sometime between when true-up testimony is received and the evidential hearings begin. So that would signal late February, early March of next year in terms of a possible, sort of, settlement time frame.

And as I sit here today, again, not having seen any direct testimony yet, but I have no reason to believe we wouldn't be able to reach agreement with the other parties in the case.

Unknown Analyst: This is Amanda on for Dave. Maybe the first point on large loads and with ESAs expected to ramp starting in the second half of '27 and then reaching full capacity in 2030. What are the main items that could accelerate or delay the ramp? And do you see any impact to earnings from any shift to the expected ramp?

Martin Lyons: Yes, look, first of all, as you probably saw in our slides, we were encouraged by the construction activity that we're seeing with respect to the 2.2 gigawatts of construction that's already underway. We showed in a couple of pictures, that's for Google and for Amazon. So we're seeing really good progress in terms of those construction activities as well as our own construction crews. It's great to be able to go out and meet with our teams that have been interconnecting the transmission assets that we have to these particular sites and have had great progress there as well. So really, it's terrific to see. So as we sit here today, we are encouraged by the signs we're seeing.

We expect ramp to begin in 2027 and as you noted, ramp aggressively in '28 and '29. What could throw that off? I would say construction delays at those sites to the extent those would occur. But frankly, we've had pretty good weather year-to-date and are seeing, again, very good progress. But I think that's the primary thing would be any delays in construction that could occur over the course of 2027 as they really look to finalize those structures. Unknown Analyst: Great. That's very helpful. And then you raised the, like, '26 range to $5.35 to $5.55. Any specific moving pieces to call out there and, kind of, what puts you into that higher range?

Martin Lyons: Yes. I think Lenny covered it really well as he went through 2026. We've had favorable weather year-to-date. We've had some favorable gains on some innovation investments that we've made. And that's been partially offset by investments that we've made, O&M investments that we've made in our system as it relates to things like additional vegetation management, energy center maintenance, things that we've really done to bolster reliability for our customers and our distribution system as well as bolster the reliability of our energy centers, which is really going to be important in the years ahead. We saw those as needed investments, frankly, very early in the year and began making those investments early.

So net, we feel very confident in our ability to raise the midpoint of our guidance $0.10.

Operator: Our next question will come from Carly Davenport with Goldman Sachs.

Carly Davenport: Maybe just starting on the revised EPS growth outlook. Obviously, the '27 guidance is just north of 8% growth year-over-year. Anything more you can share about the cadence of growth as we work through the new planning period relative to that 8% to 10% range?

Martin Lyons: Yes, that's a really terrific question and I appreciate it. First of all, as it relates to 2027, we had guided on our prior calls that we expected to deliver at the upper end of our prior 6% to 8% earnings per share growth range, and that's exactly what we're delivering today. If you look at that midpoint of that $5.70 to $5.90 guidance at $5.80, again, 8.4% growth off of the original guidance we gave for 2026, which was $5.35. So I think that should meet expectations.

Now as we look ahead to years beyond that, as we've spoken earlier, we're expecting to see a ramp rate in terms of the sales to our new customers, these hyperscalers under that 2.8 gigawatts of energy services agreements that we signed. You can see that we're already deploying more capital in 2027, and we'll be doing so again in 2028 as we really look to invest to build out the generation resources to serve those ESAs. So you're seeing both in '28 and '29, higher sales growth as well as higher rate base growth in those periods.

And as you know, that's driven by the $38.1 billion of expenditures we have, which again, was increased not only for incremental generation investments in Missouri, but also, as Michael indicated, incremental investments in transmission as well, given the long-range transmission projects that we've won and the need to begin spending capital in the latter parts of this 5-year plan to achieve the in-service dates of 2032 to 2034 for those LRTP projects. So feel good about the growth all the way out through 2031 based upon all that. Now I might take the opportunity, given your question to talk a little bit about some of the upside that we also see in our plan.

So I'd focus you on Slides 11 and 12 in particular. So as you know, today, we've signed 2.8 gigawatts of energy services agreements. And as I just said, we expect those to ramp up pretty quickly after 2027. The preferred resource plan assumed 2.9 gigawatts of sales growth by 2030. So as we said earlier today, that's what we embedded in this update today, essentially 60% sales growth in Missouri by 2030. If you look over to Slide 12, in the bottom right and the second column from the right, you see which preferred plan resources, which projects and the related CapEx we've included in the update today.

That amounts to -- if you total up that column, that amounts to 7,650 megawatts of new capacity or about an 80% increase in our installed capacity. That is the generation that we believe is needed to serve that 2.9 gigawatts of assumed growth in sales out through 2030 or 2031. But as we sit today, there's upside in our plans, both to our sales and to our rate base growth plans. If you look back on Slide 11, you'll see that we have another 5.6 gigawatts of large load interest. That's what's supported by construction agreements or interconnection agreements.

And the generation assets in the full preferred plan would allow us to serve 3.4 gigawatts by 2031 and 5 gigawatts by 2036. So if we do sign additional ESAs, depending upon the amount and the timing of those sales, we would add spending towards the addition of the resources shown in the bottom right of Slide 12 and we would be spending that in this 5-year period. So that could be, again, additive in the latter part of this 5-year plan to our sales and to our capital expenditures. I would also note that in the IRP, there was an upside case, and that's depicted in the dark blue line on Page 11.

And while it's not shown in these slides, that would require more simple cycle or combined cycle gas as well as renewables during that period of 2032 to 2034. We would need those assets to go into service. But that would also, as you know, based upon supply chain and construction time lines, that would require us to actually invest more during this 5-year period and drive rate base growth even higher. So I guess bottom line, where I'm going with this is I'm very optimistic about the future. I'm excited about the economic development opportunities that are before us, excited for the communities that we serve and the jobs that this is going to create.

But we've been conservative today in the outlook that we've provided. We've only incorporated sales based upon the ESAs that we've signed. We've only incorporated the capital expenditures for the projects needed to serve those 2.9 gigawatts of sales that we've included. And we think there's upside as we look even at the latter part of the 5-year plan in terms of sales opportunities and additional CapEx. So just building that on because we feel very good about that 8% to 10% CAGR that we provided today.

Carly Davenport: Appreciate that perspective. Super helpful. And maybe just in that same vein, you also obviously raised here the 10-year pipeline pretty significantly. Martin Lyons: Yes, it's a really good question. You're right. We feel really good about that 10-year outlook and that pipeline we have. Diana Niles: Reading the Missouri IRP, we saw listed a pipeline of over 40 data center opportunities in the company's Missouri footprint.
